headline: Wall Street clawed back most of a sharp morning sell-off on Wednesday

sections.text: Core PCE inflation (the Fed's preferred measure, which leaves out food and energy) rose to 3.3% in October, a touch above the 3.2% expected, and the US economy grew at a 4.3% annual rate in the third quarter, faster than first thought; traders now see about a 98% chance of a Fed rate rise on 9 December. At the same time the US proposed new tariffs (taxes on imports) of up to 20% on 14 trading partners including China and the EU, starting January at the earliest. Chip and AI shares took the brunt, with Nvidia down 3.9%, but bargain hunters stepped in during the afternoon and the S&P 500 closed only 0.25% lower at 7,182.78, while the VIX (Wall Street's 'fear gauge') rose 7.3% to 28.29. In Europe, which had already closed, the Stoxx 600 fell 1.1% to 626.03 and the DAX 1.3% to 24,702.13; in London, defensive shares such as Imperial Brands and Unilever rose while banks and miners fell, and the FTSE 250 lost 0.9% to 23,637.00, a four-month low. Brent crude jumped 3.5% to $94.61 a barrel after Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery, and the US 10-year yield eased to about 4.85% as money moved into bonds.

US markets are shut today for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday (at 18:00 UK time), so expect thin trading. The Bank of England publishes its Financial Stability Report today, and Severn Trent goes ex-dividend today, so its price will drop by roughly the dividend as new buyers no longer get it; NextEra follows on Friday. OPEC+ (the group of big oil producers) meets on Sunday 29 November to set 2027 output, which matters for oil after this week's jump. Next week brings Nvidia's ex-dividend date on 2 December and the US jobs report on 4 December, ahead of the Fed on 9 December (about a 98% chance of a quarter-point rise priced) and the Bank of England and ECB on 17 December (about an 80% chance of a Bank of England rise).
Your long-term plan: how investing a set amount each month and rebalancing once or twice a year turn a scary week like this into a routine one. Today's lesson goes through it, with a quiz.

standfirst: The Nasdaq had fallen as much as 4.6% on hotter US inflation and new tariff plans, but closed down just 0.6% at 23,585.80, while the Dow rose 0.3% to 50,182.95. The FTSE 100 slipped 0.4% to 10,426.94.
